limitations: All baseline windows end at their last planned observation response.
Post-exit evidence has its own action/read timestamps and never extends baseline performance.
Task metrics are network transactions, not rendered frames or audio.
Absent callbacks and unavailable timings remain unknown; repeated requests can overlap.
Three exploratory repeats cannot establish a stable P95 or causal speed improvement.
Full format families, real weak wireless/cellular, external Wi-Fi, sound/subtitles/full frames/ten-minute/PiP/competitors/Main remain open.
Read-side EOF closes only the peer write direction; it cannot by itself prove that the peer stopped reading.
A read callback observed after local finish is cleanup evidence and cannot establish an earlier peer disconnection.
Diagnostic event dates are observation timestamps, not packet-capture timestamps.
Missing read-side events remain unknown; this observation does not prove that every peer close is observable.
A pending receive may expose failures to the existing NWConnection state handler earlier; transport rules are unchanged but cross-build speed causality is not established.

All six new weak-Wi-Fi candidate requests first fetched segmentOrdinal 1; the prior slow duplicate case fetched segmentOrdinal 0. These are not the same upstream segment and do not close that original failure.
